article.name: Graphify
article.summary: Graphify is a local-first codebase knowledge graph and agent context tool. It builds a persistent graph from source, documents and media, then exposes graph queries through a CLI or MCP. A separate work-memory path stores Q&A records and derives a lessons artifact from recorded outcomes; this review describes source behavior and does not establish runtime quality or performance.

who_what.text: The official repository describes Graphify as an open-source Python CLI and MCP server for turning codebases and related documents into a queryable knowledge graph. This review covers the repository implementation; Graphify Cloud and its hosted shared-memory product are separate services and are not assessed from the open-source source tree.

architecture.text: The documented pipeline has three passes: local tree-sitter and built-in parsing for code structure; local faster-whisper transcription for audio/video; and optional model-assisted semantic extraction for documents, papers, images and transcripts. The code graph is serialized as NetworkX node-link JSON; node records include IDs, labels, file type and source file, while edges carry relation, confidence tag and source file. The graph also carries schema and producer-version metadata.

Graphify performs community detection over graph relationships rather than maintaining a separate embedding or vector index. It writes graph.json, an HTML visualization and a report under graphify-out by default. The separate work-memory feature stores timestamped Q&A Markdown records under graphify-out/memory and can derive LESSONS.md plus a .graphify_learning.json sidecar; the sidecar is an overlay and does not rewrite the structural graph.

behavior.text: Build/write: extraction creates or rebuilds the project graph from selected files. The documented update command re-extracts changed files, and content-hash caching skips unchanged files. Separately, graphify save-result writes a uniquely named Markdown Q&A record with date, question, answer, optional outcome (useful, dead_end or corrected), optional correction text, and up to ten source-node IDs. URL ingest can save a fetched source as annotated Markdown for later extraction.

Update and correction: graphify update is the documented incremental graph refresh path. Work-memory saves append separate records; the inspected save path does not edit an earlier answer. A correction is represented by a new record and negative/corrected outcome signal, then reflect aggregates it. This is not a general versioned fact store or an automatic overwrite of a previous Q&A.

Delete: the reviewed work-memory implementation has no user-facing delete or erasure operation for saved Q&A records; removal of the Markdown files is an external filesystem action. Graph rebuilding/update behavior for removed source files was not independently exercised here. The CLI supports uninstall --purge for generated graph data, but this review did not execute it and it is not a per-memory deletion audit.

Retrieval: graphify query returns a question-scoped subgraph; path traces relationships between nodes; explain summarizes a selected node. MCP exposes graph tools such as query_graph, shortest_path, get_node, get_neighbors, community and graph_stats over a selected graph.json. Reflection-derived learning annotations are attached to node output as display metadata; source code describes them as display-only.

metrics.evidence: Graph queries and path traversal are implemented, but no answer set, abstention workload or adjudicated retrieval result was run in this review.
Work-memory stores corrected outcomes and reflect scores source nodes with time decay; no correction sequence or stale-answer workload was run.
No memory deletion probe, graph purge, or post-deletion retrieval check was run.
The local CLI graph is selected by project graph path; no authenticated tenant boundary or cross-project isolation workload was evaluated.
Edges retain source-file provenance and extracted/inferred/ambiguous labels, but answer support precision and citation coverage were not adjudicated.
Hash-based incremental extraction and graph query code were inspected; no latency or freshness timings were collected.
Local graph files and optional model-assisted document extraction are documented; no tokens, provider cost, or storage volume were measured.

limits.text: This is a local source review, not a runtime assessment. The default local graph and Q&A memory are filesystem-scoped to a project directory; the reviewed community code does not provide a general authenticated tenant isolation layer. The optional HTTP MCP server is a network surface whose host, API-key and deployment configuration affect exposure.

Confidence labels communicate extraction provenance, not truth: EXTRACTED describes source-explicit relationships, INFERRED records model/resolver inference with a score, and AMBIGUOUS marks uncertain relations. These tags do not establish that a final natural-language answer is supported. Work-memory lessons use decayed positive and negative signals and a corroboration threshold, but annotations are display-only and no runtime outcome was evaluated.

The pinned README and querylog implementation disagree about query logging: the README says queries are logged by default, while current querylog.py makes logging opt-in and disabled unless a path or enable flag is set. The implementation is the inspected code evidence; this inconsistency is a documentation limitation.

No Graphify runtime, tests or benchmarks were run. Recall quality, abstention, correction accuracy, deletion leakage, project isolation, evidence support, latency, write-to-recall delay, token use, cost and storage efficiency remain unknown.

benchmark.note: No Graphify runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed for this review. Source observations and the project's benchmark definitions are not measured results.
